2280: You walked up the jet bridge at the brisk pace of someone with no idea where to go but real conviction about it.
2281: You arrived and stood very still for a second, letting the fact of a whole new place settle around your shoes.
2282: A new city, full of people who have no idea you exist and no plans to find out. Perfect. That is the job.
2283: You walked off the plane and the ground felt honored to have you, or at least it didn't complain. Close enough.
2284: Off the plane at last, and the flight shrank to a story you'd tell badly and nobody would ask to hear twice.
2285: You crossed from the plane's stale calm into the new place's loud, bright, busy business. Deep breath. Good.
2286: A moving walkway offered to carry you along, so you stood there doing nothing, briefly the fastest tired person alive.
2287: You stepped out blinking, and an unfamiliar city arranged itself around you like it had always been there. It had.
2288: You planted both feet in a brand-new place and gave it a firm, quiet nod. It did not nod back. It's busy.
2289: The jet bridge handed you to the terminal, which handed you to a city that hadn't been told you were coming.
2290: First step off the plane, and some small part of you understood you were now very far from your own kitchen.
2291: You breathed in the new place and it smelled like weather you hadn't packed for. You'll manage. You always do.
2292: You stepped off into a city humming at full speed and slid quietly into the current like you'd always been in it.
2293: The door opened, the new day poured in, and you walked into it before you were entirely ready. That's traveling.
2294: You reached the end of the bridge and the crowd scattered, each of them suddenly, urgently sure of where to go but you.
2295: A whole new place, and the only person in it who knows why you came is you. Keep it that way for now.
2296: You took three steps into the terminal and were, impressively, already unsure which way led back out.
2297: You'd been in the new place ninety seconds, and something was already trying to sell you a small bottle of water.
2298: You walked off into a city that had done perfectly fine without you for ages, and decided that was about to change.
2299: A hundred signs hung overhead, and you understood every single word and still had no idea where to go.
2300: You joined the river of people flowing toward the exit and let it carry you, steering entirely optional.
2301: A wall of people held up signs with names on them. None said yours. You waved back at all of them anyway.
2302: Two strangers ahead of you hugged like they'd invented it, and you gave them a respectful professional distance.
2303: The whole crowd inched toward the doors as one, and you inched along too, out-voted on the question of speed.
2304: Someone held a sign with a name so long it needed two hands. You quietly hoped their traveler was worth it.
2305: You looked for a sign that said 'this way, detective' and found only ones for baggage, taxis, and coffee.
2306: The exit doors opened for everyone ahead of you, closed, then opened again just for you. Polite of them.
2307: A family up ahead spotted their traveler and shrieked with joy. You applauded silently and kept walking.
2308: A long row of signs offered every direction at once, which is the most and least helpful a sign can ever be.
2309: You followed the crowd, on the reasonable theory that this many people couldn't all be lost at once.
2310: The arrivals hall was one enormous room, built at exactly the scale that makes a single traveler feel like a decimal.
2311: People at the barrier watched the doors like a very slow game where the prize was one specific relative.
2312: Nobody in the greeting crowd was there for you, which made you the only person in it free to simply leave.
2313: You asked the overhead signs a simple question, and they answered with forty arrows and no opinion.
2314: You reached a fork with two arrows pointing the very same way, and stood a moment admiring the confidence.
2315: The crowd thinned near the doors, and suddenly it was just you, a suitcase, and a very large room.
2316: A greeter kept wiping the whiteboard and writing a new name, quietly running a tiny business in pure optimism.
2317: You joined the slow shuffle toward the exit, matched everyone's pace, and briefly felt like you belonged.
2318: Signs pointed left, right, and up, and you gave each one serious thought before choosing straight ahead.
2319: The arrivals hall hummed with a hundred hellos, and you contributed to the mood by not adding a single one.
